Title: Monorepo, CI, and quality gates
Description: As a developer, I want a single monorepo with CI quality gates so every change is tested and deployable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a pull request, when CI runs, then lint, typecheck, unit tests, SAST, SCA, and secret scanning must pass before merge. | Given a merge to `main`, when the pipeline completes, then a deployable artifact and preview environment are produced. | Given a failed security scan, when the PR is reviewed, then merge is blocked and the failure is visible.

Title: Environments and infrastructure as code
Description: As a platform engineer, I want reproducible dev/staging/prod environments so deployments are predictable and auditable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a clean AWS account, when Terraform is applied, then the environment is provisioned without manual steps. | Given a configuration drift, when the nightly plan runs, then the drift is reported and alerted. | Given a production change, when it is applied, then it is logged with approver and commit SHA.

Title: Observability baseline
Description: As an on-call engineer, I want logs, metrics, traces, and alerts so I can detect and diagnose incidents.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an API request, when it completes, then a structured log with request ID and latency is emitted (no PII). | Given an error-rate spike, when the threshold is exceeded, then the on-call alert fires within 5 minutes. | Given a failing release workflow, when it stalls, then an alert and dashboard entry are created.

Title: Feature flags and runtime configuration
Description: As a product engineer, I want feature flags and runtime config so I can ship safely and disable risky features.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a flagged feature, when the flag is off, then the UI/API behave as if the feature does not exist. | Given a production incident, when an admin disables a flag, then the change takes effect within 60 seconds. | Given a flag change, when it is made, then the actor and timestamp are audited.

Title: Backup, restore, and DR runbook
Description: As a platform engineer, I want tested backups and a DR runbook so we can recover from data loss.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a database backup, when restored to a clean environment, then data integrity checks pass. | Given a documented DR scenario, when the team runs the game day, then RTO/RPO targets are measured and recorded. | Given a restore failure, when it occurs, then the incident process is triggered and the runbook is updated.

Title: Security scanning and dependency policy
Description: As a security engineer, I want automated scanning and a dependency policy so vulnerabilities are caught before production.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a new dependency, when it is added, then license and vulnerability checks run automatically. | Given a critical vulnerability, when detected, then the build fails or a time-bound exception is required. | Given a container image, when built, then it is scanned and signed before deployment.

Title: Email and password signup/login
Description: As a new user, I want to create an account and sign in securely so I can start my plan.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid email and strong password, when I sign up, then an account is created and a verification email is sent. | Given valid credentials, when I log in, then a session is created and a new-device notification is sent if applicable. | Given invalid credentials, when I try to log in, then I receive a generic error and the attempt is rate-limited and audited.

Title: Email verification and password reset
Description: As a user, I want to verify my email and reset my password safely so I can recover access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an unverified account, when I click the verification link, then my email is marked verified. | Given a reset request, when I submit my email, then a single-use, time-limited link is sent and no account existence is leaked. | Given an expired or reused token, when I use it, then the request is rejected and audited.

Title: Passkey/WebAuthn authentication
Description: As a security-conscious user, I want to sign in with a passkey so I am protected from phishing.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a supported device, when I register a passkey, then it is stored against my account and can be used to sign in. | Given a registered passkey, when I sign in, then I am authenticated without a password and the event is audited. | Given a lost device, when I revoke the passkey, then it can no longer authenticate and I can use another factor.

Title: TOTP MFA and recovery codes
Description: As a user, I want TOTP MFA and recovery codes so my account stays secure if my password is compromised.
Acceptance Criteria: Given MFA is enabled, when I log in, then I must provide a valid TOTP code. | Given I lose my authenticator, when I use a recovery code, then I can sign in and the code is invalidated. | Given repeated failed MFA attempts, when the limit is reached, then the account is temporarily locked and notified.

Title: Session and device management
Description: As a user, I want to see and revoke my sessions so I can respond to suspicious activity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given active sessions, when I open security settings, then I see device, location (coarse), and last activity. | Given a suspicious session, when I revoke it, then it loses access immediately. | Given a new device login, when it occurs, then I am notified by email and in-app.

Title: RBAC and workspace scoping
Description: As a workspace owner, I want roles and scoped permissions so the right people can help without seeing everything.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a member role, when they access a resource outside their scope, then the API returns 403 and the attempt is audited. | Given a family organiser, when they help with setup, then they cannot view sealed item contents. | Given a beneficiary, when they access the workspace, then they see only their own summary and assigned items after release.

Title: Account recovery with identity verification
Description: As a locked-out user, I want a secure recovery path so I can regain access without SMS.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a recovery request, when I provide a recovery code and verify my identity, then I can reset credentials. | Given a high-risk recovery, when identity confidence is low, then the case is escalated to support with manual verification. | Given a recovery, when completed, then all sessions are revoked and the event is audited.

Title: Admin authentication isolation
Description: As a security engineer, I want admin authentication isolated from customer auth so admin compromise is harder.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an admin user, when they sign in, then they use the admin domain with SSO/hardware key and MFA. | Given a customer session, when it accesses admin endpoints, then it is rejected. | Given an admin session, when it is idle for 15 minutes, then it expires.

Title: Guided onboarding
Description: As a family organiser, I want a guided onboarding so I understand what LifeProof does and how to start.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a new signup, when I start onboarding, then I see a plain-language explanation, time estimate, and progress indicator. | Given I leave midway, when I return, then my progress is saved and I can resume. | Given I complete onboarding, when I finish, then I land on the category dashboard with a clear next step.

Title: Create personal or family workspace
Description: As a user, I want to create a personal or family workspace so I can organize my plan.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a new account, when I choose family workspace, then a workspace is created and I become owner. | Given a workspace, when I view settings, then I can see plan, members, and data controls. | Given a duplicate workspace name, when I create another, then the system allows it but warns about confusion.

Title: Invite members and family organiser role
Description: As an owner, I want to invite family members or a helper so they can contribute without seeing everything.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an invitation, when I send it, then the invitee receives an email with an expiring link. | Given a family organiser accepts, when they open the workspace, then they can add items but cannot view sealed contents. | Given an invitation is revoked, when the invitee clicks the link, then access is denied and audited.

Title: Consent and security explainer
Description: As a user, I want to understand what LifeProof can and cannot see before I add sensitive information.
Acceptance Criteria: Given onboarding, when I reach the security explainer, then I see what is encrypted, who can access it, and what LifeProof never stores. | Given a policy update, when it occurs, then I must re-consent before continuing to sensitive areas. | Given consent, when I grant it, then the version, timestamp, and scope are recorded.

Title: Onboarding checklist and readiness score
Description: As a user, I want a checklist and readiness score so I know what to do next.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a new workspace, when I view the dashboard, then I see a checklist (add document, invite beneficiary, add trusted contact, set condition). | Given I complete a step, when I return, then the checklist updates and the score increases. | Given an incomplete plan, when I seal an item, then I see a non-anxious prompt about what is still missing.

Title: Workspace settings
Description: As an owner, I want workspace settings so I can manage name, plan, members, and data controls.
Acceptance Criteria: Given settings, when I update the workspace name, then it is reflected across the app. | Given members, when I change a role, then permissions update immediately and the change is audited. | Given data controls, when I request export or deletion, then the correct workflow starts.

Title: Category-first vault dashboard
Description: As a family organiser, I want a category-first dashboard so the vault feels like a family safe, not a spreadsheet.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a workspace, when I open the vault, then I see category cards with counts, last updated, beneficiary, and completion indicator. | Given an empty category, when I view it, then I see an encouraging prompt, not a blank screen. | Given a category, when I open it, then I see items and a clear “add” action.

Title: Create and edit vault item
Description: As a user, I want to create and edit a vault item so I can record what matters.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a category, when I create an item, then I can enter title, description, instructions, beneficiary, and condition. | Given an item in draft, when I edit it, then changes are saved and versioned. | Given a sealed item, when I try to edit it, then I must unseal with step-up auth.

Title: Dynamic type-specific forms
Description: As a user, I want forms tailored to the type of record so I know what to enter.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a bank account type, when I open the form, then I see bank name, account reference, login pointer, and instructions. | Given a document reference, when I open the form, then I can link a document and add a label. | Given a subscription type, when I open the form, then I see service, billing, cancellation instructions, and priority.

Title: Prohibited secret detection
Description: As a security engineer, I want to prevent users from storing seed phrases and private keys so LifeProof does not become a honeypot.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a text field, when the content matches a seed-phrase/private-key pattern, then the save is blocked with a plain-language explanation. | Given a user tries to bypass with a document upload, when the file is scanned, then the system warns and quarantines suspected secret files. | Given a blocked attempt, when it occurs, then the event is audited without storing the secret.

Title: Seal and unseal item
Description: As a user, I want to seal an item so it becomes part of my plan and cannot be accidentally changed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a complete item, when I seal it, then I must step-up authenticate and the item status becomes SEALED. | Given a sealed item, when I unseal it, then I must step-up authenticate and the change is audited. | Given an incomplete item, when I try to seal, then I see the missing fields and cannot proceed.

Title: Item detail and family preview
Description: As a user, I want to see exactly what my family will see so I can trust the plan.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a sealed item, when I open the detail, then I see the family-facing summary, beneficiary, and release condition. | Given multiple beneficiaries, when I preview, then I can switch between them and see their scoped view. | Given a missing instruction, when I preview, then I see a warning and a prompt to add it.

Title: Search and filter
Description: As a user, I want to search and filter my vault so I can find things quickly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given many items, when I search by title/label, then results appear within 200ms. | Given filters, when I filter by category, status, or beneficiary, then the list updates correctly. | Given no results, when I search, then I see a helpful empty state.

Title: Item history and audit
Description: As a user, I want to see the history of an item so I know what changed and when.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an item, when I open history, then I see create/edit/seal/unseal events with actor and timestamp. | Given a change, when it is made, then a version is recorded and the audit event is immutable. | Given a deleted item, when I view history, then the audit remains available per retention policy.

Title: Annual review prompt
Description: As a user, I want an annual review prompt so my plan does not become stale.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a plan older than 12 months, when I log in, then I see a “still accurate?” review prompt. | Given I confirm, when I submit, then the review date updates and an audit event is recorded. | Given I update an item, when I save, then the review is marked complete and the emergency pack is flagged for regeneration.

Title: Upload initiation and completion
Description: As a user, I want to upload documents safely so my family has the originals when needed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a supported file, when I start an upload, then I receive a short-lived presigned URL and upload directly. | Given a completed upload, when I confirm, then the document moves to SCANNING and I see progress. | Given an unsupported type or oversized file, when I upload, then I see a clear error and no object is stored.

Title: Malware scan and quarantine
Description: As a security engineer, I want every upload scanned before it is available so malware cannot reach users.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an uploaded file, when the scan is clean, then the document becomes AVAILABLE. | Given a malware detection, when the scan completes, then the document is QUARANTINED and the user is notified. | Given a scanner outage, when it occurs, then uploads remain in SCANNING and are not exposed.

Title: Encryption at rest and key wrapping
Description: As a security engineer, I want documents encrypted with per-document keys so a storage breach does not expose contents.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document, when stored, then it is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and a unique data key. | Given a data key, when stored, then it is wrapped by KMS and never written in plaintext. | Given an access request, when authorized, then the key is unwrapped only for the document service role and the operation is logged.

Title: Document metadata, labels, and linking
Description: As a user, I want to label and link documents so they are easy to find and contextualize.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an upload, when I add a label and category, then the metadata is saved and searchable. | Given a vault item, when I link a document, then both records show the relationship. | Given a document linked to a policy, when the policy is released, then the document is included per the condition.

Title: Secure preview and download
Description: As an authorized user, I want to preview or download a document securely so I can use it.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an authorized user, when they request a download, then a signed URL with a 5-minute TTL is returned. | Given a preview, when it opens, then it is watermarked and the access is audited. | Given an unauthorized user, when they request access, then the request is denied and audited.

Title: Integrity verification
Description: As a security engineer, I want document integrity checks so tampering or corruption is detected.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a stored document, when it is accessed, then its SHA-256 matches the stored hash. | Given a mismatch, when detected, then access is blocked, an incident is created, and the user is notified. | Given a restore from backup, when completed, then hashes are verified.

Title: Delete and retention
Description: As a user, I want to delete a document and understand retention so I stay in control.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document, when I delete it, then it is soft-deleted for 30 days and hidden from the vault. | Given the retention window expires, when the purge job runs, then the object and versions are deleted. | Given a legal hold, when deletion is requested, then the system explains the exception and does not purge.

Title: Document access audit
Description: As an owner, I want to see who accessed my documents so I can detect misuse.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document, when I open its access history, then I see actor, action, timestamp, and coarse location. | Given an access, when it occurs, then an immutable audit event is written. | Given an admin access, when it occurs, then a reason is required and recorded.

Title: Add and edit beneficiary
Description: As a user, I want to add a beneficiary so my family knows who should receive access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a workspace, when I add a beneficiary, then I can enter name, relationship, email, and language. | Given a minor, when I add them, then the system flags guardianship and requires a guardian/trustee. | Given an edit, when I save, then the change is versioned and affected items are shown.

Title: Invite beneficiary and capture consent
Description: As a beneficiary, I want to register and consent so I am ready when the time comes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an invitation, when I accept, then I create an account and see a plain-language explanation. | Given consent, when I grant it, then the owner sees “registered and consented.” | Given I decline, when I do, then the owner is notified and can nominate a backup.

Title: Beneficiary portal summary
Description: As a beneficiary, I want to see what I will receive without seeing the contents so I can prepare.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a registered beneficiary, when I open my portal, then I see categories/items assigned to me and instructions summary. | Given an item not assigned to me, when I view the portal, then it is not visible. | Given a change in assignment, when it occurs, then I am notified without content details.

Title: Trusted contacts and roles
Description: As a user, I want to nominate trusted contacts with specific roles so verification and support are possible.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a trusted contact, when I invite them, then I choose a role (verifier, executor, guardian, professional). | Given consent, when they accept, then they appear in the release preview and verification plan. | Given a role change, when it occurs, then the contact is notified and the change is audited.

Title: Assign beneficiaries and shares
Description: As a user, I want to assign beneficiaries per item or category so the right person gets the right access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an item, when I assign a beneficiary, then they appear in the preview and release scope. | Given multiple beneficiaries, when I set shares, then they must total 100% and the UI explains the rule. | Given a category assignment, when I add a new item, then the category default is suggested but editable.

Title: Backup beneficiary and guardian
Description: As a user, I want a backup beneficiary and guardian for minors so a release does not dead-end.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a primary beneficiary, when I add a backup, then the backup is visible in the plan. | Given a minor beneficiary, when I nominate a guardian, then the guardian must consent and is verified at release. | Given the primary is deceased/unavailable, when verification completes, then the backup is considered per the plan.

Title: Relationship change notifications and audit
Description: As a user, I want everyone affected to know when relationships change so there are no surprises.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a beneficiary change, when it is saved, then affected beneficiaries and trusted contacts are notified (without content). | Given a change, when it occurs, then an immutable audit event records actor, before/after hash, and timestamp. | Given a beneficiary removal, when it occurs, then their portal access is revoked immediately.

Title: Configure death trigger
Description: As a user, I want to release my vault on verified death so my family can act.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an item, when I choose “on death,” then the condition is saved and shown in the preview. | Given a death trigger, when configured, then the system requires at least one trusted contact/verifier. | Given no beneficiary, when I save, then the system warns and prevents sealing the condition.

Title: Configure incapacity trigger
Description: As a user, I want an optional incapacity trigger so my family can help if I cannot act.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the incapacity option, when I enable it, then I must acknowledge it requires legal evidence and is off by default. | Given an incapacity condition, when saved, then the preview explains what evidence will be required. | Given I do not enable it, when I save, then the vault remains death-only.

Title: Cooling-off configuration
Description: As a user, I want to set a cooling-off period so there is time to catch mistakes or disputes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release condition, when I configure cooling-off, then I can choose 14–90 days with a default of 14. | Given a shorter period, when I try to save, then the minimum is enforced with an explanation. | Given a change, when saved, then the release preview updates and the change is audited.

Title: Per-item conditions
Description: As a user, I want different release conditions per item so not everything is released at once.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an item, when I set a condition, then it overrides the workspace default and is visible in the item detail. | Given conflicting conditions, when I save, then the system explains precedence and asks for confirmation. | Given a category default, when I add an item, then the default is suggested.

Title: Release preview
Description: As a user, I want a plain-language preview of what will be released, to whom, and when.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a plan, when I open preview, then I see beneficiary, items, conditions, cooling-off, and required evidence. | Given a gap, when I preview, then I see a warning and a link to fix it. | Given a change, when I save, then the preview regenerates with a timestamp.

Title: Pause or cancel release
Description: As a user, I want to pause or cancel a release while I am alive so I stay in control.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a triggered release, when I pause it, then release is suspended and all parties are notified. | Given a paused release, when I cancel it, then the case closes and the vault returns to SEALED. | Given a legal hold, when I try to cancel, then the system explains that legal review is required.

Title: Initiate verification case
Description: As a claimant or ops agent, I want to open a verification case so a trigger can be reviewed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a death/incapacity trigger, when a claim is initiated, then a case is created with type, claimant, workspace, and SLA. | Given a duplicate claim, when it is detected, then the case is linked and flagged for review. | Given a case, when it is created, then the workspace owner/trusted contacts are notified per policy.

Title: Evidence checklist and upload
Description: As a claimant, I want a clear evidence checklist so I know what to provide.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case, when I open it, then I see required and optional evidence with plain-language explanations. | Given an upload, when it completes, then the evidence is encrypted, linked to the case, and marked for review. | Given missing evidence, when I submit, then the case remains in EVIDENCE_PENDING and I see what is missing.

Title: KYC identity verification
Description: As an ops agent, I want claimant and beneficiary identity verified so fraud is reduced.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a claimant, when KYC runs, then document, liveness, and sanctions/PEP results are recorded. | Given a failed KYC, when it occurs, then the case is flagged and the claimant receives a clear next step. | Given a KYC provider outage, when it occurs, then the case can proceed to manual review with a documented exception.

Title: Trusted contact attestation
Description: As a trusted contact, I want to attest to a trigger so verification has independent signals.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case, when I am asked to attest, then I receive a secure link and must verify my identity/contact. | Given my attestation, when I submit, then it is recorded with timestamp and evidence reference. | Given I decline or fail verification, when it occurs, then the case is flagged and ops follows up.

Title: Ops review queue
Description: As a verification analyst, I want a queue of cases so I can prioritize and process them.
Acceptance Criteria: Given cases, when I open the queue, then I see status, SLA, type, assignee, and risk flags. | Given a case, when I assign it to myself, then it is locked to me and the assignment is audited. | Given an SLA breach, when it occurs, then the case is escalated and the dashboard alerts.

Title: Decision and four-eyes approval
Description: As a verification analyst, I want a decision workflow with four-eyes so outcomes are defensible.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a reviewed case, when I recommend approve/reject, then a second reviewer must confirm. | Given disagreement, when it occurs, then the case is escalated to legal/senior review. | Given a decision, when it is finalized, then the rationale, reviewer IDs, and timestamp are immutable.

Title: Legal hold
Description: As a legal reviewer, I want to place a legal hold so release stops when there is a dispute or court order.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case/release, when I place a legal hold, then all release actions are blocked immediately. | Given a hold, when I add a reason and court reference, then it is recorded and visible to authorized users. | Given the hold is lifted, when I clear it, then the case resumes at the correct state with an audit event.

Title: Verification timeline and audit
Description: As an ops manager, I want a timeline of every case action so I can review quality and compliance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case, when I open the timeline, then I see every action, actor, timestamp, and evidence link. | Given an export, when I request it, then a redacted, signed PDF/JSON is generated. | Given a deletion request, when it conflicts with retention, then the legal-hold exception is applied and documented.

Title: Denial and appeal
Description: As a claimant, I want a clear denial reason and an appeal path so the process is fair.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a denial, when it is issued, then the claimant receives a plain-language reason and next steps. | Given an appeal, when new evidence is submitted, then an independent reviewer is assigned. | Given the appeal outcome, when it is decided, then all parties are notified and the audit is updated.

Title: SLA timers and escalation
Description: As an ops manager, I want SLA timers and escalation so cases do not stall.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a case stage, when the SLA approaches, then the assignee and manager are alerted. | Given a breach, when it occurs, then the case is escalated and appears on the ops dashboard. | Given an escalation, when it is resolved, then the timeline records the resolution.

Title: Create release case
Description: As a release manager, I want to create a release case from a verified trigger so delivery can begin.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a verified verification case, when I create a release, then a release case is created and linked to the evidence. | Given an unverified case, when I try to create a release, then the action is blocked with a clear reason. | Given a release case, when it is created, then the beneficiaries and scope are shown for confirmation.

Title: Cooling-off timer and notifications
Description: As a release manager, I want a reliable cooling-off period so disputes can be raised before delivery.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release case, when cooling-off starts, then the end date is stored and beneficiaries are notified. | Given the cooling-off period ends, when no dispute/legal hold exists, then the case becomes READY and ops is alerted. | Given a legal hold, when it is placed, then the timer is suspended and the hold is shown to all authorized users.

Title: Beneficiary identity re-verification
Description: As a release manager, I want the beneficiary re-verified before access so account takeover cannot steal a release.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a READY release, when the beneficiary starts, then they must complete KYC/liveness again. | Given a failed re-verification, when it occurs, then access is blocked and support is notified. | Given success, when it completes, then the verification is linked to the release case and audited.

Title: Secure release session
Description: As a beneficiary, I want a secure, time-limited session so I can access what was left for me.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a verified beneficiary, when they open the release, then a session with a 5-minute sensitive-view timeout is created. | Given inactivity, when the timeout is reached, then the session locks and requires re-authentication. | Given a session, when it is active, then all access is scoped to the beneficiary’s assigned items and audited.

Title: Deliver documents and instructions
Description: As a beneficiary, I want the documents and instructions in a clear order so I know what to do next.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release, when I open it, then I see categories with documents, instructions, and next-step guidance. | Given a document, when I download it, then the download is watermarked, audited, and time-limited. | Given an item with no instructions, when it is released, then I see a support prompt, not an empty page.

Title: Release receipt
Description: As a beneficiary, I want a receipt of what was delivered so there is a record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a completed release, when it finishes, then a signed PDF/JSON receipt with item manifest and timestamp is generated. | Given the receipt, when I download it, then it is available in my portal and linked to the audit log. | Given a partial release, when it occurs, then the receipt lists delivered and pending items.

Title: Dispute handling
Description: As a claimant, I want to raise a dispute so a release can be reviewed before it happens.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release in cooling-off, when I raise a dispute, then release is paused and legal is notified. | Given a dispute, when it is resolved, then the outcome (release/deny/partial) is recorded and all parties notified. | Given a dispute after release, when it is raised, then an incident is created and access can be revoked if warranted.

Title: Dual approval for release
Description: As a security officer, I want two approvers for every release so no single insider can release a vault.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a READY release, when one approver approves, then the case waits for a second, different approver. | Given the same user attempts both approvals, when they try, then the second is rejected and audited. | Given both approvals, when recorded, then the release proceeds and both identities are logged.

Title: Partial release
Description: As a release manager, I want to release some categories/items while others remain on hold so families get urgent help first.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release case, when I select a subset, then only those items are delivered and the rest remain pending. | Given a legal hold on one item, when partial release runs, then held items are excluded and clearly marked. | Given a partial release, when it completes, then the receipt and audit reflect the scope.

Title: Post-release access expiry
Description: As a security officer, I want release access to expire so links cannot be reused indefinitely.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release session, when it expires, then further access requires support re-verification. | Given a downloaded document, when the link expires, then it cannot be reused. | Given a re-access request, when approved, then a new audited session is created.

Title: Generate encrypted emergency pack
Description: As a user, I want an encrypted PDF summary of my plan so my family can start the process offline.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a sealed plan, when I generate a pack, then a PDF is produced with cover sheet, inventory labels, beneficiary instructions, trusted contacts, and QR code. | Given the pack, when it is generated, then it contains no passwords, seed phrases, private keys, or credential values. | Given generation, when it completes, then the event is audited and the pack is available for download.

Title: PIN protection
Description: As a user, I want the pack PIN-protected so physical loss does not expose my plan.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a pack, when I set a PIN, then the PDF is encrypted and requires the PIN to open. | Given the PIN, when I forget it, then LifeProof cannot recover it and explains this clearly. | Given a weak PIN, when I set it, then the system warns but allows it with confirmation.

Title: QR code and offline instructions
Description: As a beneficiary, I want a QR code and offline instructions so I know how to start a release.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a pack, when I scan the QR code, then it opens a signed, expiring release portal link with the workspace ID. | Given the platform is unavailable, when I follow the offline instructions, then I have a phone/email escalation path. | Given the QR code, when it expires, then the pack explains how to request a new link.

Title: Regenerate and version pack
Description: As a user, I want the pack to stay current so my family does not rely on stale instructions.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a vault change, when I save it, then the system prompts me to regenerate the pack. | Given a regeneration, when it completes, then a new version is created and the old version is marked superseded. | Given the pack history, when I view it, then I see version, date, and audit event.

Title: Transactional email
Description: As a user, I want transactional emails for security, verification, and release events so I am never surprised.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a security event, when it occurs, then an email is sent within 1 minute with plain-language next steps. | Given a verification/release event, when it occurs, then the relevant parties receive the correct template. | Given a delivery failure, when it occurs, then it is retried and surfaced in the ops dashboard.

Title: In-app notification center

Description: As a support agent, I want notes and macros so I can help consistently without exposing sensitive data.

Title: Admin reason logging

Title: Bank and exchange beneficiary links
Description: As a user, I want links to institution beneficiary processes so my family knows what to do.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an account, when I add it, then I can attach the institution’s beneficiary/claims URL and notes. | Given a release, when delivered, then the beneficiary sees the official process link. | Given a stale link, when checked, then the system flags it for review.

Title: Calendar and reminder integrations
Description: As a user, I want reminders in my calendar so reviews are not forgotten.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an annual review, when scheduled, then I can add it to Google/Outlook calendar. | Given an event, when clicked, then it opens the review flow. | Given a cancellation, when I opt out, then no further events are created.

Title: CRM integration for partners
Description: As a partner, I want CRM integration so client status flows into my systems.
Acceptance Criteria: Given HubSpot/Salesforce, when connected, then client status events sync. | Given a consent restriction, when configured, then only approved fields sync. | Given a sync failure, when it occurs, then an alert and retry are triggered.

Title: Bug bounty program
Description: As a security researcher, I want a bug bounty so I can report issues responsibly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a report, when submitted, then triage and severity are recorded within SLA. | Given a valid critical finding, when confirmed, then a reward and remediation timeline are agreed. | Given a public program, when launched, then scope and safe harbor are clear.

Title: SOC 2 Type II
Description: As a partner, I want a SOC 2 report so I can trust LifeProof’s controls.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the control set, when evidence is collected for the period, then the auditor can test it. | Given a gap, when identified, then a remediation plan and owner are assigned. | Given the report, when issued, then it is available to partners under NDA.

Title: ISO 27001
Description: As an enterprise partner, I want ISO 27001 so procurement can approve LifeProof.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ISMS, when implemented, then policies, risk register, and internal audit are in place. | Given a certification audit, when completed, then nonconformities are closed. | Given the certificate, when issued, then it is published and maintained.

Title: Open-source recovery client
Description: As a user, I want an open recovery client so I can access my export even if LifeProof disappears.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an export, when opened with the recovery client, then metadata and documents can be decrypted with the user’s key. | Given the source code, when published, then build instructions and reproducible builds are available. | Given a vulnerability, when reported, then a disclosure and patch process exists.

Title: Transparency report
Description: As a customer, I want a transparency report so I know how requests and incidents are handled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a reporting period, when published, then it covers legal requests, incidents, and releases (aggregated). | Given a sensitive case, when reported, then no PII is included. | Given a correction, when needed, then the report is versioned.

Title: Reproducible builds and code signing
Description: As a security engineer, I want reproducible builds so users can verify the client.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release, when built twice, then the artifacts match byte-for-byte or have a documented diff. | Given an artifact, when distributed, then it is signed and verified. | Given a mismatch, when detected, then the release is blocked and investigated.

Title: PWA install and offline shell
Description: As a mobile user, I want to install LifeProof and use a basic offline shell so I can access emergency info.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a supported browser, when I install, then the app launches standalone. | Given offline mode, when I open the app, then I see cached emergency info (no sensitive contents). | Given connectivity returns, when I sync, then changes are reconciled safely.

Title: Mobile document capture
Description: As a mobile user, I want to scan documents with my camera so setup is easy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given camera access, when I capture, then I can crop/rotate and upload. | Given a blurry image, when detected, then I am prompted to retake. | Given upload, when complete, then the document follows the normal scan/encrypt pipeline.

Title: Biometric login
Description: As a mobile user, I want biometric login so access is fast and secure.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a device with biometrics, when I enable it, then I can sign in with Face ID/Touch ID/fingerprint. | Given a failed biometric, when it occurs, then fallback to passkey/TOTP is offered. | Given a revoked device, when it occurs, then biometric login stops working.

Title: Push notifications
Description: As a mobile user, I want push notifications so I do not miss critical events.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a critical event, when it occurs, then a push notification is sent without sensitive content. | Given a user opt-out, when set, then non-critical pushes stop. | Given a delivery failure, when it occurs, then email/in-app fallback is used.

Title: Offline emergency card
Description: As a user, I want an offline emergency card so first responders/family can find key contacts.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an emergency card, when enabled, then it is available offline with permissioned data. | Given a lost device, when accessed, then sensitive data is minimized and protected. | Given an update, when it occurs, then the offline cache refreshes on next sync.

Title: Beneficiary mobile release
Description: As a beneficiary, I want to complete the release on my phone so I can act quickly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a release, when I open it on mobile, then identity verification and document access work. | Given a low-bandwidth connection, when I load, then progressive download and retry are supported. | Given a session timeout, when it occurs, then I can re-authenticate without losing progress.

Title: Emergency card
Description: As a user, I want a digital/physical emergency card so my family can find key contacts in a crisis.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a card, when generated, then it shows emergency contacts, allergies/medical notes (optional), and a QR link. | Given a QR scan, when authorized, then it opens a permissioned summary (no credentials). | Given a lost card, when reported, then the QR link can be revoked.

Title: Renewal and expiry reminders
Description: As a user, I want reminders for passports, insurance, and licences so my documents stay current.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document with an expiry date, when it approaches, then I receive a reminder. | Given a renewal, when I upload a new version, then the old version is archived. | Given no expiry date, when I add a document, then I can optionally set one.

Title: Life-event review triggers
Description: As a user, I want prompts after life events so my plan stays accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a life event (marriage, birth, divorce, bereavement), when I record it, then the system prompts a review. | Given a review, when I complete it, then affected items/beneficiaries are updated. | Given a missed trigger, when the annual review occurs, then the system asks about life changes.

Title: Family health score
Description: As a family organiser, I want a family health score so I can see our collective readiness.
Acceptance Criteria: Given family members, when I open the score, then I see aggregate completion without contents. | Given a gap, when identified, then I see a specific, non-anxious next step. | Given a member opts out, when they do, then their data is excluded.

Title: Family readiness report
Description: As a family organiser, I want a readiness report so I can share progress with my family.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a plan, when I generate the report, then it shows completion, gaps, and next steps without secrets. | Given a report, when shared, then the recipient sees only permitted information. | Given a change, when it occurs, then the report can be regenerated and versioned.

Title: Subscription cancellation checklist
Description: As a beneficiary, I want a subscription cancellation checklist so I can manage recurring charges.
Acceptance Criteria: Given released subscriptions, when I open the checklist, then I see service, priority, cost, and cancellation instructions. | Given a priority, when sorted, then essential services appear first. | Given a completed cancellation, when I mark it, then the checklist updates and records the action.
